“Going offline is where most successful D2C brands lose momentum”

If you’re a D2C brand looking to enter offline distribution and build real-world visibility, Priyabrata Padhi is the kind of operator from Maxinor you should be speaking to especially if the next 3 to 9 months are about turning that move into tangible revenue growth.

At Maxinor - The Venture Studio, we care a lot about operators: people who understand how things get done on the ground and execute with clarity and intent.
Across his journey, our Partner, Padhi has worked across offline distribution, consumer strategy & research, media management, digital, brand sponsorships, and experiential initiatives, along with building his own startup in the wellness and healthcare space.

The move from online traction to offline scale is where many brands slow down not because demand isn’t there, but because distribution, visibility, and on-ground execution a requires decades of consumer, cultural and market experience to be successful.  Padhi understands this from actual experience at #heineken, #ITC among others.

He brings a practical #operator lens on how to enter offline channels, build distribution, and make the brand visible where it matters, while ensuring brand, media, and consumer understanding support that journey.

Beyond work, what makes conversations with him interesting is his deep interest in history and quizzing, which shows up in how he connects dots and approaches situations.

Welcome #Padhi. Good to have him building with us.

A founder we were working with asked a simple question:
“how do we reduce our order-to-payment cycle by 7-10 days?”

To answer it, his team had to pull data from multiple places: orders, warehouse dispatch, finance, and the CRM tracking customer follow-ups. Nothing was broken, but connecting the dots took hours, sometimes days the first time.

For this venture operating with Maxinor Labs, we connected these data sources using AI tools, introduced an operational data dashboard that shows any delays instantly: stuck orders, dispatch gaps, payment follow-ups because as operators we have resident process knowledge for order-to-payment cycle. 

Once the data became visible, the start-up operations team focused on fixing other internal issues rather than defending current processes. And this operational dashboard now has evolved into a real time monitoring of the entire order to payment flow.

The start-up/ venture saved considerable amount of time and heartburn to solve this problem because Maxinor's operator philosophy is to back and solve for entrepreneurs.

Maxinor: The Studio That Builds With You, Not Just For You 

There's a version of venture that looks like this: a check, a board seat, a quarterly call. Maybe some intros and then the founder figures out the rest alone. The picture here tells what all a founder needs to carry all by himself. 

Maxinor - The Venture Studio was built because we sensed that the pure funding/investment model was not solving all problems for early-stage Venture navigating the hardest early years of their existence. And the data backs that up. 

India has the world's third-largest startup ecosystem yet 90% of Indian Venture fail within five years. 28,000+ shut down between 2023 and 2024. Seed to Series A now takes 774 days; nearly double three years ago. The leading cause isn't competition or bad timing. It's an execution gap. 

By 2025, things got harder. 11,223 shutdowns in the first ten months alone, up 30% from all of 2024. Seed to Series A wait hit 616 days. Series A to B gap reached a record 2.8 years. 

Founders have never had less room to figure it out as they go. These aren't bad ideas dying. They're execution failures. And they're largely preventable. That's exactly why we built Maxinor - The Venture Studio. We're an operator-led venture studio. What that means in practice: we don't just back Venture, we build and scale the critical operating levers that determine whether they make it. 

1. AI Infrastructure & Technology.  
2. Go-to-market.
3. Revenue operations.
4. Product Roadmap & execution 

These aren't things we advise on from a distance; these are things we own and run, shoulder to shoulder with the founders we back.  
The result speaks for itself. Venture studio Venture reach Series A at nearly double the rate of traditionally backed companies, 72% versus 42%, and get there in 25 months compared to 56 months the traditional way. 

The result is a startup that moves faster, leaner, and smarter because it has an experienced operating engine behind it from day one. That operating engine is what Maxinor - The Venture Studio is. 

Samir Gupta Amar Daing Alok Kumar Parool Duggal Rajesh Ramanathan Priyabrata Padhi Saniya Fatima Aman Sharma

"The Future with Autonomous AI Agents"

Autonomous AI Agents Are Powerful.
They’re Also a Governance Problem Waiting to Happen. One of the least discussed risks in AI today isn’t model accuracy. It’s agent behavior.

As organisations deploy autonomous AI agents at scale, we’re effectively creating a new class of “digital workers” ones that generate content, take actions, access data, and make decisions continuously.

This is why the global conversation is shifting: • OpenAI and Anthropic emphasise alignment and guardrails
• The EU AI Act focuses on risk classification and governance
• Enterprises are realising AI cannot be “set and forgotten”

At Maxinor - The Venture Studio we believe this creates a new venture category altogether: AI governance, orchestration, and trust enablement for autonomous agents.

We’re inviting AI product builders who need Operator Led Venture Studio support for GTM, Product, Fund Raise to build products/solutions for the problems autonomous AI will inevitably create not after failure, but before scale. Because the future won’t be about how powerful your agents are. It will be about how safely and predictably they operate.

#AI #AutonomousAgents #AIGovernance #VentureStudio #Maxinor #AIInfrastructure

AI Won’t Replace Large Enterprise CEOs, But it will "Redesign How Venture Are to be Built"!

Two articles today made an interesting contrast. One article at #livemint claims AI is gunning for the CEO’s job, the other by Dr. Siddharth Pai from Siana Capital reminds us that AI is still unpredictable and that the real opportunity lies in creating a layer that continuously tunes, governs, stabilises and operationalises AI. 

From these we understand that there is as an opportunity to provide "AI-as-a-managed service" or even may be even AI Operating System (AI-OS) that helps enterprises manage AI and its connected architecture so they can drive growth, operational leverage and financial gains.

Dr. Siddharth Pai perhaps also suggests that India’s IT sector could use it excellent experience in 1. Managed services, 2. Engineering depth and 3. operational discipline to create this layer of AI-as-a-managed service (AIMS)
 
At #Maxinor’s Venture Studio, we’re already seeing this shift where startup founders don’t need “AI tools"! They need orchestration of 

• Operational workflows tuned by AI tools
• Operating model monitoring and governance using AI tools
• Human-in-the-loop judgment for consistent outputs from AI tools
• GTM, revenue and retention playbooks built with AI at the core

This above is mostly likely to be the new operating architecture for Venture. 

We believe that AI-OS or AIMS needs all the above three capabities that the India IT sector possesses, to be fully leveraged by enterprises and Venture.

Finally, AI won’t replace the CEO. But the Venture that scale relatively faster will be the ones that adopt/build "AI-as-a-managed service" (AIMS) into their operating model continuously, deliberately and systemically. 

The next generation of Venture won’t use AI. They will run on it 😊 

Amar Daing Parool Duggal Samir Gupta Livemint Lounge #AI-as-a-Managed-Service #AIMS Asia EconomicTimes

Blunt take after 15+ years in the trenches: most 'growth consulting' is too safe (unrealistically so if you pay attention) to actually move the needle.
 
You get decks, frameworks, and workshops. You don't get changed pipelines, reworked pricing, or hard calls made on underperforming channels.
 
At Maxinor - The Venture Studio , we only deploy capital where we can also embed as operators. That means we sit inside the team, fix what's broken, and take accountability for the outcome.
 
I've seen great founders lose 6–12 months (and a whole lot of cash flow) on advice that looked smart but never hit the ground. Operator capital exists to close that execution gap.
 
If you're stuck (or even thinking about sustainably growing) post PMF in the ₹2 Cr–₹10 Cr ARR zone and feel like you're 'doing everything right' but not moving fast enough, that's usually the problem.
 
What's the biggest growth challenge you'd hand to an operator if you had one on your side? Let us know
